title.zh: 网格路径：自顶向下 + lru_cache

blurb.en: How many ways are there across a grid from the top-left to the bottom-right, moving only right or down and never through a blocked cell? Ask the question from each cell and let lru_cache remember the answers.
blurb.zh: 从网格左上角走到右下角、只许向右或向下、不许穿过障碍格，一共有几条路？从每一格出发各问一次，让 lru_cache 记住答案。

en: The grid is a list of strings: a full stop is an open cell and # is blocked. paths_from(r, c) answers a smaller version of the same question - how many paths are there from cell (r, c) to the bottom-right corner? Every path from a cell starts either with a step down or with a step right, so the answer is the paths from the cell below plus the paths from the cell to the right. That is why the problem splits into sub-problems so naturally.

There are two base cases. Stepping off the grid or onto a # gives 0 paths. Standing on the bottom-right cell itself gives exactly 1 path: the one that has already arrived. How recursion works in general is on the Recursion page.

Without a cache the same cell is asked about again and again: a cell in the middle is reached through many different routes. lru_cache remembers the answer for each (r, c), so each cell is worked out once and the whole grid costs about rows times cols calls. How lru_cache stores its answers is covered in Fibonacci with lru_cache; here it is only used. The inner function is defined inside count_paths, so every grid gets a fresh cache - answers for one grid are never reused for another.

This is the top-down direction: start from the big question and let the calls work their way down to the base cases. Grid Paths: Bottom-Up Table solves the same recurrence in the opposite order. On the demo grids: the open 3 by 3 grid has 6 paths, the four-by-four town grid with three blocked cells has 3, and the little grid whose bottom-right cell is blocked has 0.
zh: 网格是一个字符串列表：句点是可走的格子，# 是障碍。paths_from(r, c) 回答的是同一个问题的小一号版本——从 (r, c) 这一格走到右下角有几条路？从一格出发的任何一条路，第一步要么向下、要么向右，所以答案就是「下面那格出发的路数」加「右边那格出发的路数」。问题就是这样自然地分成了子问题。
基例有两个。走出网格或踩上 #，路数是 0。站在右下角那一格上，路数正好是 1：就是已经到达的这一条。递归本身的机制见「递归」一页。
不加缓存的话，同一格会被反复问到：中间的一格可以从许多条不同的路走过来。lru_cache 为每个 (r, c) 记住答案，每一格只算一次，整张网格大约只要 rows 乘 cols 次调用。lru_cache 怎样存答案，见「斐波那契：lru_cache 装饰器」；这里只是拿来用。内层函数定义在 count_paths 里面，所以每张网格都有一份新的缓存——一张网格的答案绝不会被另一张拿去用。
这是自顶向下的方向：从大问题出发，让调用一路往下走到基例。「网格路径：自底向上填表」用同一个递推式、反过来的顺序求解。演示里的几张网格：3 乘 3 的空网格有 6 条路；4 乘 4、有三个障碍的 town 网格有 3 条；右下角被堵住的那张小网格是 0 条。

lineNotes.at: if r >= rows or c >= cols or grid[r][c] == "#":
lineNotes.en: Off the bottom, off the right-hand side or on a blocked cell: no path from here. The two range tests come first, so grid[r][c] is only looked at when it exists.
lineNotes.zh: 从下边或右边走出了网格，或者踩在障碍上：从这里出发没有路。两个越界判断写在前面，grid[r][c] 只在确实存在时才去看。

lineNotes.en: A fresh cache for every call of count_paths, because the decorated function is created inside it.
lineNotes.zh: 每调用一次 count_paths 就有一份新缓存，因为被装饰的函数是在它里面新建的。

title.zh: 网格路径：自底向上填表

blurb.en: The same grid question answered the other way round: fill in a table of path counts cell by cell, row by row, starting from the top-left.
blurb.zh: 同一个网格问题反过来答：从左上角开始，一行一行、一格一格填出一张路数表。

en: ways[r][c] holds the number of paths from the top-left corner to cell (r, c). The last step into a cell comes either from the cell above or from the cell to its left, so its count is the sum of those two counts. This is the same recurrence as in Grid Paths: Top-Down with lru_cache, turned round: that version asks about the paths from a cell to the goal, this one about the paths from the start to a cell.

The order of filling matters. Row by row, left to right, means that by the time a cell is reached, the cell above and the cell to the left are already finished. No recursion and no cache are needed - the table is the memory.

The edges are where the care goes. A blocked cell is skipped with continue and keeps its 0, so nothing flows through it. The start cell is set to 1. Cells in the first row have no cell above them and cells in the first column have nothing to their left, so each of the two additions has its own if that only runs when that neighbour exists. Without those two tests, r - 1 on the first row would be -1, and Python would quietly read the last row instead of raising an error.

Every cell is visited once, so the work is rows times cols. The demo grids give the same answers as the top-down version: 6 paths across the open 3 by 3 grid, 3 across the town grid and 0 when the bottom-right cell is blocked.
zh: ways[r][c] 存的是从左上角走到 (r, c) 这一格的路数。走进一格的最后一步，要么从上面那格来、要么从左边那格来，所以它的路数就是这两格的路数之和。这和「网格路径：自顶向下 + lru_cache」是同一个递推式，只是反过来：那一版问「从这一格到终点」，这一版问「从起点到这一格」。
填表的顺序很要紧。一行一行、每行从左到右，保证轮到一格时，它上面和左边那两格都已经填好。不需要递归，也不需要缓存——这张表本身就是记忆。
要小心的是边界。障碍格用 continue 跳过、保持 0，什么都流不过它。起点那一格设成 1。第一行的格子上面没有格子，第一列的格子左边没有格子，所以两次相加各有自己的 if，只在那个邻居存在时才执行。少了这两个判断，第一行的 r - 1 会是 -1，Python 不会报错，而是悄悄读到最后一行。
每一格只访问一次，工作量是 rows 乘 cols。演示网格的答案与自顶向下版相同：3 乘 3 的空网格 6 条路，town 网格 3 条，右下角被堵住时 0 条。

lineNotes.en: A blocked cell keeps the 0 it started with, so no paths are counted through it.
lineNotes.zh: 障碍格保持一开始的 0，不会有路从它这里被数进去。

lineNotes.en: The start cell: one way to be here, which is to have just started. It is open, because a blocked start was skipped above.
lineNotes.zh: 起点：待在这里只有一种方式，就是刚出发。它一定可走，被堵住的起点在上面已经跳过了。

lineNotes.en: The paths whose last step comes in from the left.
lineNotes.zh: 最后一步从左边进来的那些路。

blurb.en: Each item has a weight and a value, and each can be taken at most once. Which ones give the greatest value without going over the capacity? A table answers it for every number of items and every capacity.
blurb.zh: 每件物品有重量和价值，每件最多拿一次。拿哪几件，才能在不超重的前提下价值最大？一张表把「前几件、多大容量」的每种情形都答一遍。

en: best[i][w] is the greatest value that can be made from the first i items with capacity w. Row 0 means no items are allowed, so it is all 0, and so is column 0, where nothing fits. The answer to the whole question is the bottom-right cell, best[n][capacity].

Each new item gives exactly two choices, which is where the name 0/1 comes from: leave it (0) or take it once (1). Leaving it means the best is whatever the first i - 1 items could do with the same capacity - the cell directly above. Taking it is only possible if it fits; then it adds its value, and the other items have weight less capacity to work with, so the rest of the value comes from the row above, weight columns to the left. The cell keeps the larger of the two.

Why the row above and never the same row: the same row already allows item i, so reading from it could take item i a second time. Row i - 1 is guaranteed to be without it. weights[i - 1] and values[i - 1] are item i, because the table rows start counting at 1 while the lists start at 0.

The table has (n + 1) times (capacity + 1) cells and each takes a constant amount of work. Trying every subset instead would mean 2 to the power n subsets. In the demo, with weights 3, 4 and 5 and values 5, 6 and 8: capacity 9 gives 14 (the items weighing 4 and 5), capacity 7 gives 11 (3 and 4), and capacity 2 gives 0, because nothing fits.
zh: best[i][w] 表示：只用前 i 件物品、容量为 w 时能拿到的最大价值。第 0 行代表一件都不许拿，全是 0；第 0 列代表什么都装不下，也全是 0。整个问题的答案在右下角那一格 best[n][capacity]。
每来一件新物品，只有两种选择，0/1 这个名字就是这么来的：不拿（0），或者拿一次（1）。不拿，最好的就是前 i - 1 件在同样容量下能做到的——正上方那一格。拿，得先装得下；装下后加上它的价值，其余物品能用的容量少了 weight，所以剩下那部分价值从上一行、往左 weight 列的那一格来。这一格留下两者中较大的。
为什么总是看上一行、而不看同一行：同一行已经允许拿第 i 件了，从它读就可能把第 i 件拿第二次。第 i - 1 行保证不含它。weights[i - 1] 与 values[i - 1] 就是第 i 件，因为表的行从 1 数起，列表的下标从 0 数起。
表一共 (n + 1) 乘 (capacity + 1) 格，每格只花常数时间。要是逐个试所有子集，就是 2 的 n 次方个。演示里重量 3、4、5，价值 5、6、8：容量 9 时是 14（拿重 4 和重 5 的两件），容量 7 时是 11（重 3 和重 4），容量 2 时是 0，什么都装不下。

lineNotes.en: One row per number of items allowed (0 to n), one column per capacity (0 to capacity).
lineNotes.zh: 每行对应允许拿的件数（0 到 n），每列对应一种容量（0 到 capacity）。

lineNotes.en: Taking item i is only a choice when it fits into capacity w on its own.
lineNotes.zh: 只有第 i 件单独放得进容量 w，「拿」才是一个选项。

lineNotes.en: All n items allowed, full capacity: the answer to the whole question.
lineNotes.zh: n 件全都允许、容量用满：整个问题的答案。

blurb.en: The same knapsack with a single list instead of a table. It only works if the capacities are visited from the largest down to the smallest.
blurb.zh: 同一个背包问题，用一个列表代替整张表。只有容量从大到小走，它才是对的。

en: In 0/1 Knapsack: 2D Table, every row is worked out only from the row just above it. So one row is enough, provided it is updated in place: before item i is processed, best[w] holds the old row (the best without item i); after, the new one.

The direction is the whole trick. Taking the item at capacity w reads best[w - weight], a smaller capacity. Walking from high to low means that smaller capacity has not been updated yet for this item, so it still holds a value that does not include the item - exactly the row above in the table version. Each item can therefore be taken at most once.

Walk from low to high instead and best[w - weight] has already been updated for this item, so it may already contain it: the item can be taken again and again. That is a different problem, the unbounded knapsack. On the demo items it shows: with capacity 9 the low-to-high order would answer 15, by taking the weight-3 item three times, while the correct 0/1 answer is 14.

The work is the same as the table's, (number of items) times (capacity), but the memory drops from a whole table to one row of capacity + 1 numbers. The demo gives the same answers as the table version: 14 for capacity 9, 11 for capacity 7 and 0 for capacity 2.
zh: 在「0/1 背包：二维表」里，每一行只由它正上方那一行算出来。所以一行就够了，前提是原地更新：处理第 i 件之前，best[w] 存的是旧的一行（不含第 i 件时的最好值）；处理完，就是新的一行。
关键全在方向。在容量 w 处拿这一件，要读 best[w - weight]，一个更小的容量。从大往小走，那个更小的容量在这一件上还没被更新过，存的仍是不含这一件的值——正好就是表格版里的上一行。于是每件最多拿一次。
反过来从小往大走，best[w - weight] 在这一件上已经更新过，里面可能已经拿了它：这一件就能被拿一次又一次。那是另一个问题——完全背包。演示里的物品就能看出来：容量 9 时，从小往大走会得到 15（把重 3 的那件拿三次），而正确的 0/1 答案是 14。
工作量和表格版一样，件数乘容量；但内存从一整张表降到一行 capacity + 1 个数。演示的答案与表格版相同：容量 9 是 14，容量 7 是 11，容量 2 是 0。

lineNotes.at: for weight, value in zip(weights, values):
lineNotes.en: One item at a time; zip pairs each weight with its value.
lineNotes.zh: 一次处理一件物品；zip 把每个重量和它的价值配成一对。

lineNotes.en: best[w] on the right is still the old value (without this item); best[w - weight] is too, because smaller capacities have not been reached yet.
lineNotes.zh: 右边的 best[w] 还是旧值（不含这一件）；best[w - weight] 也是，因为更小的容量还没走到。

blurb.en: The longest run of characters that appears in both strings in the same order, though not necessarily side by side. A table gives its length; walking back through the table gives one such subsequence.
blurb.zh: 两个串里都按同样顺序出现（不必挨着）的最长一串字符。一张表给出它的长度；在表里倒着走一遍，就拿到其中一条。

en: A subsequence keeps some of the characters in their original order and drops the rest; unlike a substring, the kept characters do not have to be next to each other. table[i][j] is the length of the longest common subsequence of the first i characters of a and the first j characters of b. Row 0 and column 0 stand for an empty prefix, so they stay 0.

Look at the last characters of the two prefixes. If they are the same, that character can end a common subsequence, so the length is one more than the cell diagonally up and to the left. If they are different, at least one of them is not used, so the best is the larger of dropping a's last character (the cell above) and dropping b's (the cell to the left).

The table only holds lengths, but it remembers enough to rebuild an answer. one_lcs starts at the bottom-right cell and retraces the decisions: matching characters are collected and the walk steps diagonally; otherwise it moves towards whichever neighbour kept the larger length. The letters come out last first, which is why they are reversed at the end. When the two neighbours tie, either way leads to a longest subsequence - so the answer is one LCS, not the only one.

Filling the table takes len(a) times len(b) steps. In the demo, ABCBDAB and BDCABA have a longest common subsequence of length 4, and the walk back finds BCBA; HUMAN and CHIMPANZEE also share 4 characters in order, HMAN; ABC and XYZ share none, so the length is 0 and the subsequence is the empty string.
zh: 子序列是保留一部分字符、保持原来的先后次序、丢掉其余的；和子串不同，留下来的字符不必挨在一起。table[i][j] 是 a 的前 i 个字符与 b 的前 j 个字符的最长公共子序列长度。第 0 行和第 0 列代表空前缀，保持 0。
看两个前缀的最后一个字符。相同，这个字符就可以作为一条公共子序列的结尾，长度是左上对角那一格加一。不同，至少有一个用不上，于是取「丢掉 a 的最后一个字符」（上面那格）与「丢掉 b 的最后一个字符」（左边那格）中较大的。
表里只存长度，但记下的东西足够重建出一个答案。one_lcs 从右下角出发，把当初的决定倒着走一遍：字符相同就收下它、往左上对角走；否则往两个邻居里长度较大的那边走。字母是从后往前收集的，所以最后要反过来。两个邻居一样大时，往哪边走都能得到一条最长的——所以得到的是一条 LCS，不是唯一的那条。
填表要 len(a) 乘 len(b) 步。演示里，ABCBDAB 与 BDCABA 的最长公共子序列长度是 4，倒着走找到的是 BCBA；HUMAN 与 CHIMPANZEE 也有 4 个字符按顺序共有，是 HMAN；ABC 与 XYZ 一个都不共有，长度是 0，子序列是空串。

lineNotes.en: Same last character: use it, and add one to the answer for both prefixes without it.
lineNotes.zh: 最后一个字符相同：用上它，在两个前缀都去掉它时的答案上加一。

lineNotes.en: Step towards the neighbour that kept the longer length; on a tie this goes up, which is one of the valid choices.
lineNotes.zh: 往长度较大的那个邻居走；一样大时往上走，这是合法选择之一。

lineNotes.en: The length is the bottom-right cell: all of a against all of b.
lineNotes.zh: 长度就是右下角那一格：整个 a 对整个 b。

blurb.en: The fewest single-character inserts, deletes and replacements needed to turn one string into another - the number behind spell-checkers' suggestions.
blurb.zh: 把一个串变成另一个串，最少要几次单字符的插入、删除、替换——拼写检查给建议时背后就是这个数。

en: dist[i][j] is the edit distance between the first i characters of a and the first j characters of b. The first column is turning a prefix of a into the empty string, which takes one delete per character, so it counts 0, 1, 2 and so on; the first row is building a prefix of b from nothing, one insert per character.

For any other cell, think about the last operation. Deleting a's last character leaves the cell above, plus 1. Inserting b's last character leaves the cell to the left, plus 1. Replacing a's last character with b's leaves the cell diagonally up-left, plus 1 - or plus 0 if the two characters are already the same, which is what cost records. The cell takes the smallest of the three.

The table's indices are one ahead of the strings': row i stands for a's first i characters, so its last character is a[i - 1]. Getting that off by one does not crash in most places, because a[-1] is a legal index in Python - it just quietly compares the wrong characters. The answer is the bottom-right cell, the whole of a against the whole of b, and filling the table takes len(a) times len(b) steps.

In the demo, turning kitten into sitting takes 3 edits (replace k with s, replace e with i, insert g at the end); flaw into lawn takes 2 (delete f, insert n); building abc from the empty string takes 3 inserts, and a string is 0 edits from itself.
zh: dist[i][j] 是 a 的前 i 个字符与 b 的前 j 个字符之间的编辑距离。第一列是把 a 的前缀变成空串，每个字符删一次，所以是 0、1、2……；第一行是从无到有造出 b 的前缀，每个字符插一次。
其余每一格，想想最后一步操作是什么。删掉 a 的最后一个字符，剩下的是上面那一格，再加 1。插入 b 的最后一个字符，剩下的是左边那一格，再加 1。把 a 的最后一个字符替换成 b 的，剩下的是左上对角那一格，再加 1——两个字符本来就相同时加 0，cost 记的就是这个。这一格取三者中最小的。
表的下标比串的下标领先一位：第 i 行代表 a 的前 i 个字符，它的最后一个字符是 a[i - 1]。这里差一位，多数地方并不会报错，因为 a[-1] 在 Python 里是合法下标——只是悄悄比错了字符。答案在右下角那一格，整个 a 对整个 b；填表要 len(a) 乘 len(b) 步。
演示里，kitten 变成 sitting 要 3 次（k 换成 s、e 换成 i、末尾插入 g）；flaw 变成 lawn 要 2 次（删掉 f、插入 n）；从空串造出 abc 要插入 3 次；一个串和它自己的距离是 0。

lineNotes.en: Building the first j characters of b from nothing: j inserts.
lineNotes.zh: 从无到有造出 b 的前 j 个字符：插入 j 次。

lineNotes.en: Delete a's last character: the cell above, plus one operation.
lineNotes.zh: 删掉 a 的最后一个字符：上面那一格，再加一次操作。

lineNotes.en: The cheapest of the three ways the last operation could go.
lineNotes.zh: 最后一步的三种走法里最省的那一种。

lineNotes.en: All of a against all of b.
lineNotes.zh: 整个 a 对整个 b。

blurb.en: Give change by always taking the biggest coin that still fits. With UK coins that always uses the fewest coins; with other coin sets it can go wrong.
blurb.zh: 找零时每次都拿还放得下的最大面值。用英镑硬币时，这样用的枚数总是最少；换一套硬币就可能出错。

en: A greedy algorithm makes the choice that looks best right now and never goes back on it. Here that means: look at the coins from largest to smallest, and take each one as many times as it fits into what is left. sorted with reverse=True makes a new list in that order and leaves the caller's coins list as it was.
The coins are in pence, so 288 is £2.88. The demo gives it as 200, 50, 20, 10, 5, 2 and 1 - seven coins - and 40 as two 20s. count_coins just counts the list that greedy_change builds.

For UK coins (1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50, 100 and 200) the greedy answer is always the smallest number of coins possible. That is a property of this particular set of coins, not of greedy algorithms. The last line of the demo uses coins of 1, 3 and 4 to make 6: greedy grabs the 4 first and then needs two 1s, three coins in all, although two 3s would do it with two. Once the 4 is taken, greedy never reconsiders it.
For a coin set where greedy can fail, see Coin Change: Dynamic Programming, which tries every last coin at every amount and finds 2 for the same example.
zh: 贪心算法每一步都做眼下看起来最好的选择，而且做了就不反悔。这里就是：面值从大到小看，每种面值在剩下的金额里能放几枚就拿几枚。sorted 加上 reverse=True 按这个顺序排出一个新列表，调用者传进来的 coins 保持原样。
硬币按便士计，288 就是 £2.88。演示里它被找成 200、50、20、10、5、2、1——七枚；40 是两枚 20。count_coins 只是数一数 greedy_change 拿出来的列表有几枚。
对英镑硬币（1、2、5、10、20、50、100、200），贪心给出的枚数总是可能的最少。这是这一套硬币的性质，不是贪心算法的性质。演示最后一行用 1、3、4 三种硬币凑 6：贪心先抓 4，再要两个 1，一共三枚；可两枚 3 就够了。4 一旦拿了，贪心就不会回头再想。
会让贪心出错的硬币组合，要用「找零：动态规划」：它在每个金额上把每一种「最后一枚」都试一遍，同一个例子得到 2 枚。

lineNotes.en: Values in pence, from 1p up to the £2 coin.
lineNotes.zh: 面值以便士计，从 1p 到 £2 硬币。

lineNotes.en: What is left still has to be made up by the same or smaller coins.
lineNotes.zh: 剩下的还要用同样大或更小的硬币凑出来。

blurb.en: The fewest coins for any coin set, worked out for every amount from 0 upwards - and -1 when the amount cannot be made at all.
blurb.zh: 任意一套硬币下的最少枚数：从 0 开始每个金额都算一遍——根本凑不出时返回 -1。

en: best[a] is the fewest coins that make exactly a. Making 0 needs no coins. For any other amount, whatever the best way is, it has a last coin; take that coin away and what is left is a smaller amount made in the best way. So best[a] is the smallest, over every coin that fits, of the best for a minus that coin, plus one for the coin itself. The amounts are filled from 1 upwards, so every smaller amount is already known.

impossible is amount + 1. Every coin is worth at least 1, so no amount up to amount ever needs more than amount coins; amount + 1 is a value no real answer can have. Places that cannot be made keep it (adding a coin to impossible only gives something bigger, which min never keeps), and at the end it is turned into -1.

Unlike Coin Change: Greedy, this tries every coin as the last one at every amount instead of trusting the biggest. With coins of 1, 3 and 4, it finds that 6 needs only 2 coins (3 and 3), where greedy took three. With UK coins it agrees with greedy: 288p needs 7 coins.
With coins of 2 and 4 only even amounts can be made, so 7 gives -1; making 0 always takes 0 coins. The work is amount times the number of coin values.
zh: best[a] 是恰好凑出 a 的最少枚数。凑 0 不用硬币。其余每个金额，不管最好的凑法是什么，它总有最后一枚；拿走这一枚，剩下的就是用最好方式凑出的一个更小的金额。所以 best[a] 就是：在每种放得下的硬币里，取「a 减去它」的最好枚数的最小值，再为这一枚加一。金额从 1 往上填，更小的金额总是已经算好。
impossible 是 amount + 1。每枚硬币至少值 1，所以不超过 amount 的金额最多用 amount 枚；amount + 1 是任何真实答案都不可能取到的值。凑不出的格子一直保持它（在 impossible 上再加一枚只会更大，min 不会留下它），最后再把它换成 -1。
和「找零：贪心」不同，这里在每个金额上把每种硬币都当作最后一枚试一遍，而不是只信最大的那枚。用 1、3、4 三种硬币时，它算出 6 只要 2 枚（3 和 3），贪心却用了三枚。用英镑硬币时它与贪心一致：288p 要 7 枚。
只有 2 和 4 两种硬币时，只凑得出偶数，所以 7 得到 -1；凑 0 永远是 0 枚。工作量是金额乘以硬币种数。

lineNotes.en: A stand-in for 'cannot be made' that is bigger than any real answer and is still an int.
lineNotes.zh: 代表「凑不出」的值：比任何真实答案都大，而且仍是整数。

lineNotes.en: A coin bigger than the amount cannot be the last coin.
lineNotes.zh: 比金额还大的硬币不可能是最后一枚。

blurb.en: One room, many bookings: choose the largest number that do not overlap. Sort by finishing time and take every booking that fits - the greedy choice that is provably right.
blurb.zh: 一个房间、许多预约：选出最多个互不重叠的。按结束时间排序、能放就放——这个贪心选择可以证明是对的。

en: Each activity is a (start, end) pair. Sorted by finishing time, the rule is simple: take an activity if it starts no earlier than the last chosen one ended. Because the chosen ones are taken in order of finishing time, only the last one can clash with a newcomer, so a single variable, last_end, is enough. An activity that starts exactly when the previous one ends does not overlap it.

Why the earliest finish is the right greedy choice: among all activities, the one that finishes first leaves the room free the soonest. Any best schedule can swap its first activity for this one without clashing with anything else, so taking it never loses. The same argument then applies to what is left.

Two other greedy rules sound just as sensible and are wrong. The demo list long_first has (0, 10), (1, 3) and (4, 6): taking the earliest start picks (0, 10), which blocks both others - 1 activity - while finishing-time order takes (1, 3) and (4, 6), 2 activities. The list short_middle has (0, 5), (4, 7) and (6, 11): taking the shortest first picks (4, 7), which overlaps both others - 1 activity - while finishing-time order takes (0, 5) and (6, 11), 2.
The longer demo list of eight bookings gives 3: (1, 4), (5, 7) and (8, 11). Sorting takes O(n log n) and the scan is a single pass. count_activities just counts the chosen list.
zh: 每个活动是一个 (start, end) 二元组。按结束时间排好后，规则很简单：一个活动开始时，上一个已选的已经结束，就选它。已选的活动是按结束时间先后收进来的，能和新来者冲突的只可能是最后那一个，所以一个变量 last_end 就够了。恰好在上一个结束时开始的活动，不算和它重叠。
为什么「最早结束」是对的贪心选择：所有活动里最先结束的那个，让房间最早空出来。任何一个最优安排，都可以把它的第一个活动换成这一个，而不和其余任何活动冲突，所以选它永远不吃亏。剩下的部分再照同样的道理推下去。

另外两条听起来同样有道理的贪心规则是错的。演示里的 long_first 是 (0, 10)、(1, 3)、(4, 6)：按最早开始选，先拿 (0, 10)，它把另外两个都挡住了——只有 1 个；按结束时间选，拿到 (1, 3) 和 (4, 6)，2 个。short_middle 是 (0, 5)、(4, 7)、(6, 11)：按最短先选，先拿 (4, 7)，它和另外两个都重叠——只有 1 个；按结束时间选，拿到 (0, 5) 和 (6, 11)，2 个。
较长的那份八个预约的演示列表，选出 3 个：(1, 4)、(5, 7)、(8, 11)。排序是 O(n log n)，之后只扫一遍。count_activities 只是数一数选中的列表。

lineNotes.en: The key for sorting: the second item of the pair, its end.
lineNotes.zh: 排序用的键：二元组的第二项，也就是结束时间。

lineNotes.en: None means nothing has been chosen yet, so the first activity always fits.
lineNotes.zh: None 表示还一个都没选，所以第一个活动一定放得下。

lineNotes.en: From now on, the next activity must start no earlier than this one ends.
lineNotes.zh: 从现在起，下一个活动的开始不能早于这一个的结束。

blurb.en: How many bits does Huffman coding need for a piece of text? Merge the two rarest groups again and again; every merge makes each character in them one bit longer. No tree is built.
blurb.zh: 用 Huffman 编码，一段文字要几位？反复合并最少见的两组；每合并一次，组里每个字符的码长就加一位。不建树。

en: Huffman coding gives common characters short codes and rare ones long codes. The usual picture is a tree, but only the code lengths matter for the total, so this program keeps just a length for each character. First it counts how often each character appears.

Every character starts as its own group, paired with its count, and the groups go onto a heap. The heap is only used here as a priority queue: whatever order things went in, taking an item off it always gives the one with the smallest count. The loop takes out the two rarest groups and merges them. In the tree, merging two groups puts both under a new parent, which adds one bit to the code of every character inside them - so each of their lengths goes up by one. The merged group goes back with the two counts added.

When one group is left, each character's length is final, and the total is its count times its length, added up. With only one kind of character there is nothing to merge; by convention each character still needs one bit, so the answer is simply the length of the text. The empty text needs 0 bits.

In the demo, abracadabra needs 23 bits: a (5 times) gets 1 bit, r (2 times) 2 bits, b (2 times) 3 bits, and c and d (once each) 4 bits. Stored as 8-bit characters it would take 88 bits. aaaaaaab needs 8 bits, one per character; abcdefgh, where all eight characters are equally common, needs 24 - 3 bits each, no better than a fixed-length code. zzzz needs 4 and the empty string 0.
zh: Huffman 编码给常见字符短码、给少见字符长码。通常的画法是一棵树，但总位数只取决于每个字符的码长，所以这个程序只为每个字符记一个长度。第一步先数出每个字符出现几次。
每个字符先自成一组、配上它的次数，所有组放进一个堆。这里堆只当优先队列用：不管放进去的顺序如何，从堆里取出一项，得到的总是次数最小的那一项。循环每次取出最少见的两组、合并成一组。在树里，合并两组就是给它们安上一个新的父结点，组里每个字符的码字都多出一位——所以它们的码长各加一。合并后的组带着两个次数之和放回堆里。
只剩一组时，每个字符的码长就定了，总位数是每个字符的次数乘码长、再加起来。只有一种字符时没什么可合并；按惯例每个字符仍要 1 位，所以答案就是文字的长度。空串是 0 位。
演示里，abracadabra 要 23 位：a（5 次）1 位，r（2 次）2 位，b（2 次）3 位，c 和 d（各 1 次）4 位。按每字符 8 位存要 88 位。aaaaaaab 要 8 位，每个字符 1 位；abcdefgh 八个字符一样常见，要 24 位——每个 3 位，并不比定长编码好。zzzz 要 4 位，空串 0 位。

lineNotes.en: Count each character; get gives 0 the first time a character is seen.
lineNotes.zh: 数每个字符；某个字符第一次出现时，get 给出 0。

lineNotes.at: heap = [(n, [ch]) for ch, n in counts.items()]
lineNotes.en: Each group is (count, list of its characters). The count comes first, so the heap orders groups by it.
lineNotes.zh: 每一组是（次数, 它的字符列表）。次数放在前面，堆就按它排序。

lineNotes.at: return sum(counts[ch] * length[ch] for ch in counts)
lineNotes.en: Each character costs its code length once for every time it appears.
lineNotes.zh: 每个字符每出现一次，就要花一次它的码长。
